slots.jd.title: Propulsion Engineer
slots.jd.meta: Hybrid, distributed; test work onsite · $115,000-$155,000 base salary + equity

jd.intro.html:
We build connected hardware, and the propulsion team is small: a handful of engineers and one hardware partner. You would own a propulsion subsystem, not a slice of one.

The work is hands-on in the way propulsion always is. You will spend more time on what the hardware does on the test stand than on a clean analysis deck. Hot-fires fail, sensors lie, and someone has to find out why before the next build. That is the job, and it is also why people here stay.

slots.jd.close: Direct space-propulsion experience is not required and is not an edge in our screen. The same problem, controlled high-energy fluid and thermal systems on flight-critical hardware, shows up in gas-turbine and jet-engine work, automotive and motorsport powertrain, and high-pressure process systems. We have hired from those fields, and those engineers are among our strongest. If that is you, apply.
slots.jd.benefits: Base range reflects the posted location. Compensation also includes equity, health coverage, retirement plan, and paid time off. Open until filled.
slots.jd.eeo: We are an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will be considered without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable law. If you need an accommodation to apply or interview, tell your recruiter.
slots.s2.title: What we changed from intake
slots.s2.body: Every change from the hiring manager's first draft, with its pool consequence. Pool counts are Estimates off the BLS-OES 17-2011 base (BLS OEWS May 2024 national employment for SOC 17-2011), each filter applied to the reachable propulsion subset. Bring this if any line gets challenged.
slots.caution.1: If the flight-heritage requirement is restored, the posted band no longer clears the experienced market where the shortage bites hardest, and the search reverts to a 90-day, relocation-dependent profile. Those two are one decision, not two.
slots.gate.1: No eligibility or work-authorization line is posted. Adding one goes through counsel, not the hiring manager.
slots.s3.title: Where the base band lands
slots.s3.body: Published base band against the national market for the same title and a comparable stage of company. The role is distributed, so the benchmark is national, not one metro.
slots.comp.readout: Read-out: the posted band sits inside the sourced band and reaches toward its upper half, fair for a small non-prime employer. This is an Estimate, not a survey: BLS-OES 17-2011 P25-P75 ($105K-$174K) blended with a second published aerospace source ($112K-$172K; name it when you fill this). Expect to win on scope, cadence, and equity, not top-of-market cash. Say that in the screen, not at offer.

jd.responsibilities.resp.item: Design and analyze a propulsion subsystem end to end: what it must do, how it is sized, how it is verified.
Own hot-fire and thrust-stand test: build the setup, instrument it, run it, and reduce the data into decisions.
Thermofluids and combustion, or electric-propulsion analysis: CFD, FEA, and thermal models the hardware then confirms or refutes.
Work the interfaces: feed system, structures, avionics, and the one external hardware partner. A few weeks a year on console through test campaigns.

jd.requirements.req.item: Propulsion system design in at least one type: liquid, solid, hybrid, or electric. You have taken a design from requirements to real hardware.
Real command of thermofluids: thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, and heat transfer applied to high-energy hardware in production or test settings.
Hands-on propulsion test: hot-fire or thrust-stand work, test-stand instrumentation, and turning raw runs into clean data reduction.
CAD plus analysis fluency: CFD, FEA, or thermal modeling in a standard toolchain, for example ANSYS, Siemens NX, or SolidWorks.
You have owned a subsystem end to end on flight or test hardware, including the parts nobody scoped, from requirements through verification.

annotations.note.body: Team size and the hardware partner are in the first two lines. For a small propulsion team, "own a subsystem, not a slice" is the strongest promise in the post.
The test-stand line is deliberate. Naming that hot-fire and hardware work is hands-on and mostly onsite raises reply quality and kills a late-stage surprise.
Long requirement lists suppress applications, including from the adjacent-industry engineers we most want. Everything cuttable was cut to five.
This search ships no work-authorization or clearance line. Propulsion often carries one in the wider market; this role does not, so none was invented or implied.
The last paragraph converts adjacent-industry engineers, powertrain, gas-turbine, motorsport, who would otherwise self-reject. It is the highest-yield sentence in the file.
